title: Bound sessions, rotation, revocation, and outage behavior
description: Change lifetimes, refresh strategy, revocation enforcement, key overlap, and incident condition. The model exposes the stale-access window, affected boundary, and operational decision.

refreshStrategies.label: No refresh token
refreshStrategies.detail: Run a new authorization flow after the access token expires.
refreshStrategies.replayBoundary: No refresh credential exists; access-token replay remains a separate concern.

refreshStrategies.label: Reusable bearer refresh
refreshStrategies.detail: One refresh credential can be presented repeatedly until expiry or revocation.
refreshStrategies.replayBoundary: A copied token has no built-in reuse signal and can reach the session ceiling.

refreshStrategies.label: Rotating token family
refreshStrategies.detail: Every successful refresh invalidates the old token and records family lineage.
refreshStrategies.replayBoundary: Reuse of an invalidated family member revokes the active family and forces authorization again.

refreshStrategies.label: Sender-constrained refresh
refreshStrategies.detail: The client must prove possession of a bound key when refreshing.
refreshStrategies.replayBoundary: The token alone is insufficient; combined loss of token and proof key still requires revocation.

revocationModes.label: Offline JWT verification
revocationModes.detail: The API checks signature and claims without consulting current grant state.
revocationModes.availabilityPosture: Cached known keys tolerate an issuer outage, but revocation waits for token expiry.

revocationModes.label: Local deny-before feed
revocationModes.detail: The API consumes session or subject invalidation events into local state.
revocationModes.availabilityPosture: Requests stay local; protection depends on bounded event propagation and stale-feed handling.

revocationModes.label: Online introspection
revocationModes.detail: The resource server asks the authorization server whether the token is active.
revocationModes.availabilityPosture: Current state is available at request time, but the protected path depends on the authority and any cache.

incidentConditions.label: Steady state
incidentConditions.detail: No known compromise or control-plane outage.

incidentConditions.label: Planned signing-key rotation
incidentConditions.detail: A new key signs tokens while the old public key remains available for overlap.

incidentConditions.label: Issuer outage after new kid
incidentConditions.detail: A verifier receives a token signed by a key it has not cached and cannot refresh.

incidentConditions.label: Stolen refresh token replay
incidentConditions.detail: An attacker presents a copied refresh credential from this grant.

incidentConditions.label: Signing-key compromise
incidentConditions.detail: An attacker may mint tokens that fit expected claims while the key remains trusted.

assumptions: The stale-access value is a planning upper bound after revocation is recorded; detection time is outside the model.
For rotation arithmetic, the longest old-key access token equals the selected access-token lifetime.
A token using an unseen kid fails closed. A verifier never follows an arbitrary key URL from the token.
The selected lifetimes and propagation values are design inputs, not vendor defaults or universal recommendations.
